thread:
acme_ops: Hi team — our March 10th dedicated pool shows ~48 GPU hours billed but our token dashboard only reports ~120k tokens. This doesn't match expected throughput. Can you help?

maria_s: Hey, sorry you're seeing that. Can you paste the pool id and the invoice line or billing export rows you see?

acme_ops: Pool ID: pool-cc-42. Invoice extract attached earlier (CSV): line shows 48.2 reserved_gpu_hours for Mar 10-11. Attached raw metering CSV shows very low token counts on those hours.

maria_s: Thanks. Can you also share a couple of request IDs from that window or any request samples that should have consumed tokens?

acme_ops: Sure — request ids: r-83f4, r-83f5, r-83fd — all were low volume test spikes, <2k tokens each. We can share more if needed.

maria_s: @jake_b can you pull the metering service logs for pool-cc-42 around 2026-03-10 22:00-02:00 UTC? Also pulling infra ups/downs for that node group.

jake_b: Looking now. I see a spike in "gpu_alloc" events at 2026-03-10T22:13:02Z and again at 22:37. There are also multiple "reserve_start" entries that match the invoice granularity.

jake_b: Quick note — billing counts reserved GPU hours on node lease timestamps, not tokens. So if a node was up for the hour, that hour is billed even if token consumption low. But 48 hours in single day still looks high.

ana_i: (typo) @ana_i — checking autoscale/eviction.

ana_i: Sorry — my bad, meant @ana_i.

ana_i: Found something: pool-cc-42 had a misconfigured autoscaler policy applied on Mar 10 due to a config rollout. Min_replicas got bumped from 1 -> 8 for ~4h by a stale canary policy. That would explain the reserved GPU hours.

acme_ops: That seems plausible. We did a canary traffic test earlier but not aware of replica changes. Any evidence in rollout history?

jake_b: I'll attach the deploy bot logs.

billing-bot: deploy-rollout: canary-policy-apply by chris_p at 2026-03-10T21:58:44Z -> set min_replicas=8 for pool-cc-42.

chris_p: Confirmed — I pushed a config change to test an autoscale heuristic; I forgot to pin the canary to a test pool. My bad, that applied to pool-cc-42 for ~4h before rollback at 2026-03-11T02:10Z.

maria_s: Ok that matches. So customer saw low token usage but we still reserved 8 GPUs for that time window. Billing system correctly charged for reserved GPU hours.

acme_ops: Understood — is there an SLA credit or adjustment process for accidental internal rollout mistakes like this? We pay for the pool but the allocation was due to your internal config bug.

jake_b: For cases where Redwood's control plane rollout caused unexpected capacity, we escalate to billing for review. @jake_b to open a ticket with timestamps & rollout id, request pro-rated credit for 4.2 hours on pool-cc-42.

jake_b: Filed internal billing ticket #BILL-2026-873. Attaching meter export, deploy bot logs, and node uptime csv.

maria_s: Also adding steps for repro/audit: 1) run metering export for pool (console -> Billing -> Exports -> select pool id + hour range) 2) query infra events: SELECT * FROM node_events WHERE pool_id='pool-cc-42' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-10T21:00Z' AND '2026-03-11T03:00Z'; 3) cross-check deploy-rollout logs for canary-policy-apply.

acme_ops: Thanks — we'll wait for the billing team. Can you confirm this won't affect our SLA credits or dedicated performance guarantees?

maria_s: SLA is based on availability/latency SLOs. Since the extra capacity increased availability (not decreased), SLA metrics shouldn't be negatively impacted. But billing credit is separate.

ana_i: (again typo) sorry. @ana_i: From infra POV, no customer-facing errors or throttles were caused. Performance was normal.

acme_ops: Ok. Quick ask: can you add an alert to warn if min_replicas > 4 on customer pools unless explicitly labeled test=true? This would prevent future accidental promos.

chris_p: Agree — I'll push a policy change: canary rollouts will be scoped to pools with label rollout=canary. Also add a billing-safecheck that flags unusual replica jumps for shared/dedicated pools and sends an automated notice to SRE and Billing.

maria_s: Next actions summarized: - jake_b: follow up with billing ticket and credit request - chris_p: implement rollout scoping + billing-safecheck - ana_i: add a monitoring alert for replica jumps - maria_s: notify customer when billing decision made (BILL-2026-873).

acme_ops: Appreciate the quick investigation and clear next steps.

maria_s: Thanks everyone — reassigning to billing; I'll update thread when there's movement. :thumbsup:

billing-bot: billing-update: ticket BILL-2026-873 status=awaiting-review assigned=jake_b

acme_ops: Received — keeping this thread open for the credit result.

maria_s: (final) Billing approved pro-rated credit for 4.17 hours on pool-cc-42; customer balance updated. Closing after invoice reconciliation.

acme_ops: Confirmed credit applied; thanks for the quick turnaround.
